source.title: Bridging the Bosphorus: Advancing Turkish Large Language Models through Strategies for Low-Resource Language Adaptation and Benchmarking
source.authors: Emre Can Acikgoz; Mete Erdogan; Deniz Yuret

record.tranche_reason: Tests parameter scaling in Turkish models using held-out bits-per-character (BPC), a loss-derived measure, and reports downstream task scores across model sizes; it does not fit the original scaling-law curves.
record.gate_note: The study reports BPC for four from-scratch Hamza model sizes and ARC-TR and TruthfulQA-TR accuracy for those models. It does not fit power laws, estimate exponents, extrapolate from smaller runs, or compare compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Results for continued Turkish pretraining and English-task forgetting do not measure held-out pretraining loss or the parameter-scaling behavior in the claim. External-model comparisons are not scaling sweeps of those models.
record.test_reason: The study trains four Turkish GPT-2-style models from scratch (124M–1.3B, all on 300B tokens) and reports held-out BPC and downstream accuracy for each. This is a parameter sweep in a new setting (Turkish, about 2.3 epochs over 130B unique tokens), so its own numbers bear on V1 and V6. It fits no power law, exponent or extrapolation, and it is not aimed at scaling laws, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right: the authors draw no scaling-law conclusion. Their main conclusions are different. Continued pretraining of a strong base (Mistral-7B) works best for Turkish but causes catastrophic forgetting of English skills. From-scratch training beats continued pretraining within the GPT-2 architecture. Current Turkish LLMs lag well behind English counterparts. They also report Hamza-xl and Kanarya-2b as having the best BPC on trnews-64.
record.recipe_differences: Turkish models trained from scratch in GPT-2-style configurations; fixed 300B-token training; evaluated with BPC on Turkish news rather than the original scaling-law loss fits.

fits_no_version.finding: During LoRA continued pretraining of Mistral-7B and GPT2-xl on 0.1–5GB of Turkish, English ARC accuracy falls steadily as Turkish data grows (Mistral 61.52→45.90).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued pretraining on a new language degrades original-language downstream skill in proportion to the amount of new-language data.

record.problems: The parameter range is 124M to 1.3B, and the paper reports no fit, uncertainty estimates, or extrapolation from small runs. BPC is a loss-derived measure, not a reported cross-entropy value. Downstream benchmarks cover only the reported Turkish tasks and show non-monotonic results across sizes.
record.rows_left_out: External models in Table 4 are comparative evaluations, not model-size scaling runs conducted in this study. Continued-pretraining English-task scores in Section 5.3 are omitted because they concern English-skill retention during Turkish adaptation, not held-out pretraining loss or the claim's parameter-scaling results.

untested.parts: Token and compute scaling; any power-law fit or exponent; ranges beyond about one order of magnitude in parameters.
All: no extrapolation from small runs.
All: tokens fixed at 300B for every size; no compute-optimal analysis.
All: shape is not varied at fixed parameter count (the xl shape change is a confound, not a test).
Fitted loss scaling for repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer. The continued-pretraining data sweep reports only accuracy, not a loss power law.
Any fit relating downstream accuracy to size or loss; extrapolation.

missing.what: ARC-TR accuracy of Mistral as a function of continued-pretraining Turkish tokens (50M–2.5B). It is shown only as a figure, with no values in the text, and is a downstream-versus-data curve in a transfer regime.

trnews-64 BPC for the XGLM family measured by the study (564M 1.125, 1.7B 1.044, 2.9B 0.946, 4.5B 0.949, 7.5B 0.880). This is a size series of one external family on a new held-out set, with a plateau at 2.9B→4.5B. rows_left_out declares it, but a researcher may want it.

record.verdict_notes: The sweep spans only about one order of magnitude in parameters at a fixed 300B tokens. The corpus has 130B unique tokens, so the models see repeated data, and Hamza-xl's architecture departs from the GPT-2 scaling pattern (24 layers, d=2048). Both are possible causes of the flattening at 1.3B. ARC-TR scores sit near chance for every Hamza size, so downstream signals are weak. The log-log slopes cited are computed from Table 4, not reported by the authors.

versions.untested_parts: Only parameter scaling is examined, across 124M to 1.3B parameters, with training tokens held at 300B. No power-law fit or exponent is reported; token and compute scaling are not tested.
No fit relating downstream accuracy to scale or pretraining loss, and no extrapolation, is reported.

rows.subject: Hamza-small
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out BPC across from-scratch model sizes; each Hamza model was trained for 300 billion tokens.
rows.note: A point in the parameter sweep; the paper reports no power-law fit.
rows.check: Smallest point of the sweep; it is the reference, not a test of an effect by itself. Baseline should read 'none (sweep anchor)'.

rows.subject: Hamza-medium
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out BPC across from-scratch model sizes; each Hamza model was trained for 300 billion tokens.
rows.note: A point in the parameter sweep; the paper reports no power-law fit.
rows.check: BPC falls 0.897→0.814 (124M→354M). In log-log terms that is a slope of about −0.09, consistent with a power-law decline. Baseline should be r1 (0.897).

rows.subject: Hamza-large
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out BPC across from-scratch model sizes; each Hamza model was trained for 300 billion tokens.
rows.note: A point in the parameter sweep; the paper reports no power-law fit.
rows.check: BPC falls 0.814→0.760 (354M→772M), a log-log slope of about −0.09, the same as the previous step. Baseline should be r2.

rows.subject: Hamza-xl
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out BPC across from-scratch model sizes; each Hamza model was trained for 300 billion tokens.
rows.note: The BPC declines across the reported size sweep, with a small change between Hamza-large and Hamza-xl; the paper reports no power-law fit.
rows.check: BPC moves only 0.760→0.754 (772M→1.3B), a log-log slope of about −0.015: the curve flattens sharply. The xl model also changes shape (24 layers, d=2048, versus 36 layers for large) and follows a different, CroissantLLM-inspired recipe, which confounds the size effect. Baseline should be r3.

relationships.condition: Hamza-small to Hamza-large (124M–772M), 300B tokens, trnews-64 BPC
relationships.reason: BPC falls steadily (0.897→0.814→0.760), with a roughly constant log-log slope of about −0.09 (r2, r3). No fit is reported; the slope is computed here from Table 4.
relationships.display_finding: Bits per character decreased from 0.897 to 0.814 to 0.760, implying a roughly constant log-log slope of −0.09 without a reported fit.

source_check.condition: Hamza-small to Hamza-large (124M–772M), 300B tokens, trnews-64 BPC
source_check.reason: Table 4 values in r1–r3 yield approximately equal adjacent log-log slopes, supporting the form within this limited range; the paper reports no fit.

relationships.condition: Hamza-large to Hamza-xl (772M→1.3B), with xl using a different shape and recipe, on about 2.3 epochs of repeated Turkish data
relationships.reason: BPC barely moves (0.760→0.754), so the curve bends away from the earlier slope. This may reflect the recipe change or data repetition; the study does not separate these (r4).
relationships.display_finding: BPC decreased only from 0.760 to 0.754, with recipe changes and data repetition left as unresolved explanations.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Hamza-large to Hamza-xl (772M→1.3B), with xl using a different shape and recipe, on about 2.3 epochs of repeated Turkish data
source_check.reason: The decline becomes much weaker in r3–r4 (0.760→0.754). Table 3 and Section 3.2 confirm architecture and training differences; the study does not isolate their effects or those of repetition.

relationships.reason: Accuracy rises only slightly from chance (25.26→29.10) and then dips at 1.3B (28.24), so improvement is weak and non-monotonic (r5–r8).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy rose from 25.26 to 29.10 before falling to 28.24 at 1.3B, remaining only modestly above chance.

relationships.reason: Accuracy does not improve with size (43.65, 43.55, 40.93, 42.33) even though BPC falls, so downstream score does not track loss here (r9–r12).
